title: Pin every release-script npm call to the public registry, and read back the launcher readme after publish
description: Follow-up from confirming QCLI-399 AC4 against lore-cli LCLI-621, read by ref at opum-ai/lore-cli bb8b2662 (dev tip; #337 squash, tree identical to reviewed head e9213411). Lore does two things quest does not; neither is part of the agreed flow contract. (1) REGISTRY PINNING. Every lore npm write and read passes --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/ AND --@opum-ai:registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/ (their REGISTRY_PINS), with reads also passing --userconfig=/dev/null. Reproduced here on npm 12.1.0: with a project .npmrc setting @opum-ai:registry to a dead host, `npm view @opum-ai/quest@0.11.0 version --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/` fails ECONNREFUSED, and adding the scope flag succeeds. So --registry alone does not override a scope registry. Quest dist-tag READS are already pinned (anonymous fetch by URL, QCLI-390). But publish (publish-release.mjs publishArgs, promote-release.mjs launcherPublishArgs), npm dist-tag add (promote-release.mjs setTag), npm view (isPublished, bundle-integrity registryHoldsTarball, pair-receipt observe, release-provenance, native-execution-receipt) and npm pack (downloadServedTarball) all run unpinned. package.json has no publishConfig. This machine sets no scope registry (npm config get @opum-ai:registry: undefined), so the exposure is latent: an npmrc carrying @opum-ai:registry would receive the write or answer the read. (2) README READ-BACK. Lore promote-latest.mjs readBackReadme re-reads `npm view <launcher> readme` after the X publish until it is non-empty (it lags; LCLI-460 measured ~25 min). QCLI-399 AC3 is that same measurement, currently manual.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Every npm publish, dist-tag add, view and pack in scripts/ that targets @opum-ai packages passes both --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/ and --@opum-ai:registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/, and a test fails if a call site omits either
A test or measurement shows a project .npmrc setting @opum-ai:registry elsewhere does not redirect a pinned release-script call
promote-release.mjs reads back npm view @opum-ai/quest readme after the X publish, retrying through registry lag, and reports its byte count; an unreadable read is reported as unknown, never as 0

implementationNotes: Implemented 2026-09-28 on feat/QCLI-400-registry-pins-readme. REGISTRY_PINS (scripts/qualification/registry-visibility.mjs) holds --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/ plus --@opum-ai:registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/, the same pair as lore REGISTRY_PINS. Applied at every registry-reaching npm call in scripts/: publishArgs, launcherPublishArgs, dist-tag add, npm pack <spec>, npm stage list, and npm view in 7 places (isPublished, registryHoldsTarball, pair-receipt, release-provenance, native-execution-receipt, the build-candidate-bundle rc lookup, and the new read-back). Also applied to release.yml: both staging npm publish lines and the visibility npm view. The 4 local-only calls (pack of a directory, install of local tarballs) are allowlisted by name. SCAN: the test reads 14 npm argument-list literals (10 pinned, 4 local) and fails below 10, so an empty scan cannot pass. It cannot see Bun.$ template spawns or non-literal argv; the two non-literal publish sites are covered by testing their builders. AC2 MEASURED OFFLINE: `npm config get @opum-ai:registry`, in a directory whose .npmrc points the scope at a dead host, returns the dead host unpinned (the positive control) and with --registry alone, and returns registry.npmjs.org with both pins (npm 12.1.0; the test re-runs it in CI). README READ-BACK: readBackReadme runs `npm view @opum-ai/quest readme` pinned, up to 10 times at 15s, and stops at the first non-empty read; it runs after the GitHub Release is cut and only reports, as lore does. DOES IT CATCH THE EMPTY-PACKUMENT CASE (OPAG-474 AC3): YES. Measured 2026-09-28 on 0.11.0, key set printed first: the packument has a readme key present as an EMPTY string (readmeFilename also empty, the 0.11.0 version object has no readme key), and npm view @opum-ai/quest readme prints 0 bytes with exit 0. The read-back reports that as 0 bytes plus a WARNING, and an unreadable registry as null ("unreadable"), never 0. Lore packument reads the same (readme length 0). Caveat: 10x15s covers about 2.5 min against the ~25 min lore measured, so a 0 at promote time is more often lag; the warning prints the re-measure command. bun run check: 854 pass. Six mutation controls each turned red only their predicted tests. A first harness run falsely showed all green: unquoted $T in zsh passed three test paths as one argument, so 0 tests ran. It was caught because an all-clean mutant set is implausible, and re-run with an array that prints the test count.
